newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA SEES 18 PCT HIV INFECTION RATE BY YR 2000.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA SEES 18 PCT HIV INFECTION RATE BY YR 2000.

text.p: Four percent of Botswana's population, currently estimated at some 1.5 million people, will have full-blown AIDS by the year 2000, according to projections released by the state health authority.

Rose Mandevu, the coordinator of the AIDS/STD Unit of the Ministry of Health, told a weekend seminar that the social and economic consequences of AIDS were likely to deepen over the next few years as the disease spread.
"Recent projections show that by the year 2000, four percent of the population will have AIDS and 18 percent will be HIV infected," Mandevu said.
"No studies have yet been done in Botswana to assess the macro-economic and social impact of HIV/AIDS. Such a study is long overdue."

The most economically active sectors of the population are worst affected by the spread of the human immunodeficiency virus, which leads to AIDS. Figures show Botswana citizens aged 15 to 49 account for 89 percent of all reported cases. Of this, more than half (56 percent) are youths aged 15 to 29.
A national policy on HIV/AIDS was developed in Botswana in 1993, eight years after the first confirmed case of AIDS. The disease was also given the status of a national crisis.
United Nations figures show 14 million people in sub-Saharan Africa have AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome).
